prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Boundary: receiving interface through completed outbound-load release; pallets remain inside through inspection, identification, buffering, storage, retrieval, dispatch preparation. Objective: accurate processing and committed dispatch times without bypassing safety/inventory controls. No explicit modes.
Warehouse Management System (Morrowglass): authoritative inventory/status/location/eligibility and work release; maintains expected inbound shipment data; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment for outbound-planning changes. Inventory-moving work requires authorized release; movements/status must reconcile. Allocation follows recorded shipment count, inspection status, door release; evaluates dimensions, mass, compatibility, retrieval demand. Locations support safe handling, efficient retrieval, inventory controls.
Yard Gate Controller (Velvetrook): controls perimeter access; records vehicle identity, carrier, trailer number, arrival time; directs cleared trailers from staging to assigned doors. Drivers follow gate instructions. Check scheduled delivery window before assignment; review unscheduled arrivals before receiving entry. Assign doors only with door, staging lane, unloading crew available; coordinate yard positions to avoid traffic obstruction. Unavailable doors require safe holding pending confirmed reassignment.
Inbound Inspection Desk (Cinderbay): checks paperwork against expected shipment, confirms trailer presentation; promptly records outcomes before storage; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note for seal follow-up. Staff verify trailer identifiers/seals before unloading authorization; record damage/mismatches/compromised seals with shipment details; compare pallet count/paperwork before unloading completion; segregate damaged pallets. Acceptance requires valid receipt instruction and safe handling. Monitor door occupancy/clearance; pause unloading for unsafe conditions/documentation conflicts/equipment issues. Yard personnel notify receiving staff of departure readiness. Receiving closes after count/status/door-release recording.
Pallet Dimension Scanner captures eligibility dimensions; Inbound Pallet Buffer holds accepted pallets pending storage.
North Aisle Stacker Crane/South Aisle Stacker Crane serve respective aisles; East Transfer Conveyor/West Transfer Conveyor serve respective routes; Conveyor Line Controller coordinates scoped movement; Autonomous Forklift Fleet uses approved areas/authorized tasks.
Outbound Dispatch Sorter sequences eligible pallets; Outbound Checkweigh Scale verifies precompletion weight; Shipping Documentation Desk prepares load records.
Warehouse Operations Supervisor oversees exceptions/priorities/recovery and escalated receiving issues. Safety Zone Controller restricts protected-area movement; Fire Alarm Panel supplies alarm status; Maintenance Release Terminal records availability.

Document units:
S053: Fast-moving inventory is generally assigned to positions that support short travel paths to its next handling step.
S054: Pallets with restricted handling requirements are assigned only to positions approved for those conditions.
S055: The allocation logic preserves clearances for the pallet and the equipment needed to access it.
S056: A position is excluded when its capacity, status, or operating restrictions conflict with the pallet profile.
S057: The Warehouse Management System produces the Slot Reservation Receipt.
S058: A reservation remains subject to confirmation that the selected position and its access path are available for operation.
S059: The reservation record identifies the selected position and the conditions used to validate its suitability.
S060: Crane operations are divided into aisle zones to limit conflicting equipment movement.
S061: Each stacker crane normally retrieves and stores pallets within its assigned aisle boundaries.
S062: The North Aisle Stacker Crane is also known by the alias Juniperwake.
S063: The North Aisle Stacker Crane serves storage positions in the north aisle and follows the aisle's configured travel limits.
S064: The South Aisle Stacker Crane serves its assigned storage positions under equivalent travel and access controls.
S065: Cross-aisle movement is controlled so that crane travel does not extend beyond authorized operating zones.
S066: Crane commands are issued only when the target position and the required aisle conditions are valid.
S067: The Pallet Dimension Scanner is also known by the alias Moonquarry.
S068: The Pallet Dimension Scanner measures pallet height, width, and length before storage suitability is finalized.
S069: The measured profile is checked against configured dimensional limits and the declared pallet profile.
S070: The Pallet Dimension Scanner produces the Oversize Load Advisory.
S071: The dimension advisory identifies a measured profile that exceeds an applicable storage or handling limit.
S072: An advisory does not by itself authorize placement in a position that fails the storage rules.
S073: The Warehouse Management System can retain the measured dimensions with the pallet's inventory record for later allocation decisions.
S074: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor can review unresolved allocation conditions through established operational procedures.
S075: Inbound pallets enter the conveyor area only after the preceding inspection and identification steps are complete.
S076: The East Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along the eastern approach to the transfer area.
S077: The West Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along the western approach to the transfer area.
S078: The Conveyor Line Controller sequences pallet movement across the available conveyor sections.
